audit.whatIsWrong: The page framed Levels 1-3 as Ryze's window and the late game as Mundo's raid-boss window. That is backwards and it contradicts the packet level chart, the content whys[] and the 59.05% Emerald+ win rate.
audit.why: Ryze pays 40 mana per Overload, 50 for a rank-1 Rune Prison and 35 for Spell Flux, and none of that out-damages Mundo's regen at levels 1-3. Ryze's real windows are Levels 4-5 (E-W root plus a jungler) and the late game once his mana stacks.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-3 Dr. Mundo, Levels 4-5 Ryze, Level 6 skill, first item Dr. Mundo, 2+ items Ryze — matching the packet chart and whys[].

audit.why: Spike entries already read Lvl 3-5, Lvl 6, 1st item, Late with a genuine 4th entry, and they agree with the corrected chart: Mundo bullies early, even at 6, owns the first-item window, loses the scaling race.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated, and Rune Prison was described as a 'point-blank root' on a '14s' cooldown.
audit.why: Rune Prison is a 615-range targeted cast on 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 — not point-blank and not 14s. Riot's text says it only roots if the target already has Flux on them; otherwise it is a slow. A slow does not trip Mundo's passive, but the Flux-empowered root does — Mundo resists it and drops a cannister he can walk over to heal and cut the passive's cooldown. So Ryze's entire lockdown pattern costs him E plus W and buys him nothing on the first attempt.
audit.corrected: Rune Prison (11s at rank 1, 9s maxed, 615 range) roots only through Spell Flux; Mundo's passive eats that first root and drops a healing cannister. Infected Bonesaw's 975 range out-ranges both W and E (615), so Mundo pokes from outside his entire lockdown range.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects flagged zero cooldown-sequencing advice, and the one cooldown number on the page was wrong.
audit.why: The punishable window is the 9-11 seconds after Rune Prison is spent, and Mundo's own trade clock is Heart Zapper's 17s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Step up the moment W is spent; trade on Heart Zapper's 17s recast.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood was generic template text about 'heavy crowd control' with no Ryze-specific trigger.
audit.why: Against Ryze the only CC that trips Mundo's passive is the Flux-empowered Rune Prison, and Mundo's Q out-ranges it by 360 units.
audit.corrected: Poke from 975, step in after W is spent, cannister-heal through the root.

audit.why: Nothing in the brief establishes a 26.15 change to either champion, and I will not assert one without a source.

edits.after: Overload costs 40 mana and your regen eats it — you win the straight level 1. Bonesaw from 975 outranges Rune Prison's 615, so poke, last-hit, and make him spend mana.

edits.before: Still Ryze's window. Heart Zapper absorbs a chunk of burst and pays it back — take only the trades where your W can cash its damage store.
edits.after: Heart Zapper absorbs his burst and pays it back on recast, and its 17s cooldown is your trade clock — go at 2 while his mana pool caps him at Q-E chip.

edits.before: Full kit online and your passive shrugs the first CC. Cleaver poke plus E-empowered swats start the grind; never brawl while Rune Prison is up.
edits.after: Rune Prison only roots if Spell Flux is on you first, and your passive eats that root and drops a cannister — grab it, then run him down while W sits 11s.

edits.before: Q ranks make the cleaver chunk real HP and your passive regen ramps. Ryze must kill you through the sustain or watch you out-scale — most can't.
edits.after: His window: Rune Prison is 11s and Flux costs 45 mana, so he can chain the E-W root into a jungler. Once your cannister is spent, hold your side of the wave.

edits.before: Warmog's makes you a raid boss: full HP between every fight. Ryze needs Grievous Wounds and a jungler to even slow you down — split, soak, win.
edits.after: Ryze's window: mana stacking makes Flux-Overload chunk even a Warmog's bar, and Rune Prison pins you for his team. Split and soak — don't duel him.

edits.after: - Ryze Rune Prison (11s at rank 1, 9s maxed): matchup-defining — it only roots through Spell Flux, and your passive eats that root. Step up the moment W is spent. - Your ultimate (120s): spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call.

edits.after: Track Rune Prison (11s): it roots only through Spell Flux, and your passive eats the first root. Go when W is spent.

edits.after: See the level-by-level chart — fight in your windows (Levels 1-3 and first item), respect his (Levels 4-5, and 2+ items).

edits.before: Line up your trajectory cleanly past enemy minion models. Launch an Infected Bonesaw (Q) to slow and chunk their current health, then step forward only when they are slowed to execute a quick auto-attack into an enhanced Blunt Force (E) reset. If they retaliate with heavy crowd control, your passive will pop a canister backward—walk over it immediately to heal up and walk away clean.
edits.after: Stand outside 615 so Rune Prison and Spell Flux can't reach you, and throw Infected Bonesaw (Q) from 975 on its 4s cooldown — you pay no mana for it, and he pays 40 a cast, so his pool drains first. Step in only after he spends W: his root needs Flux on you, and your passive eats that root and drops a cannister — walk over it, then E-reset him and leave.
